minutes.headline: Finance Committee recommended a reserve fund transfer for the school 911 cabling; the preliminary budget was delayed to Feb 27.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a school department request for a reserve fund transfer to cover unbudgeted enhanced 911 cabling and voted by roll call to recommend it. The new town manager explained why no preliminary budget was presented (revenue estimate errors, local receipts, capital funding) and aimed for Feb 27. The IT department presented its FY26 budget items, and the committee approved minutes and previewed upcoming meetings.

votes.motion: Recommend transferring from the reserve fund to the school department contracted services and computers purchase and lease line items for the 911 cabling project
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; members voted aye, chair announced it passes)

budget_items.what_was_said: Districts out of compliance can face fines per day, which is why the project was pursued.
figures_as_heard: up to 10,000 plus 500 a a day

budget_items.what_was_said: Total project cost was described as unbudgeted; the later explanation says the original budget covered only part and the rest was added when existing cabling proved inadequate.

budget_items.topic: Original vendor requote vs state bid quote
budget_items.what_was_said: The original vendor requoted higher, so the district got a lower quote from the state bid list.
The reserve fund was set at the previous annual town meeting for the committee to release; part was already released for the town manager search.
After the request the reserve would have roughly the stated remainder for the rest of the year.
Chair stated two transfer amounts, from the reserve fund to contracted services and to computers purchase and lease.
The town manager said there was a math error in the revenue estimates and the 2.5 percent was not applied to the levy including the override, leaving more revenue than thought.
Local receipts were estimated by an average; the town manager wants a deeper look to be less conservative.
Capital funding uses tax levy plus one-time funds under a draft financial policy not yet adopted.
The MUNIS contract will rise as the system moves to the cloud; software maintenance also rises with inflation.
Upgrading DPW to a faster connection costs a small amount more per year and will be requested in FY26.
Construction alone to bring fiber into DPW was quoted at a figure; IT will first try faster coax.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted by roll call to recommend a reserve fund transfer to the school department for unbudgeted enhanced 911 cabling.
The town manager did not present a preliminary budget, citing errors in the revenue estimates, and hopes to present the full budget on Feb 27.
The town manager said the 2.5 percent increase was not applied to the levy including the override, which leaves more revenue than first thought.
The IT department presented its FY26 budget items, including a rising MUNIS contract as the system moves to the cloud.
Departments were asked to supply full budgets with prior-year actuals in a standardized Excel format.

why_it_matters: The reserve fund was set at Town Meeting for the committee to release, so each transfer, including this one, leaves less in it for the rest of the year.
The FY26 revenue estimate has changed since it was first built, and the preliminary budget that residents and Town Meeting will vote on comes later than first expected.
watch_next: Feb 27: the town manager hopes to present the preliminary budget and capital plan, with DPW, facility and sewer.
Feb 20 (Council on Aging, Public Access, Library) and Feb 25 (police, fire, land use): department budget hearings.
